entities.summary:
Western Sahara is a sovereign nation in North Africa, Africa. Its capital is El Aaiún (Laayoune) (de facto, Moroccan-administered) / Tifariti (SADR declared capital). Official languages include Hassaniya Arabic, Standard Arabic. Government: Disputed territory (majority administered by Morocco; Polisario/SADR controls eastern strip). Population: approximately 0.6 million.

Area: 266,000 km². Comprehensive index for Western Sahara (disputed territory) covering Saharan rock art, Sanhaja Berber nomads, Almoravid movement origin, trans-Saharan trade, Spanish Sahara colonisation, phosphate discovery, Green March 1975, Polisario Front, SADR (Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic), Moroccan Wall/Berm, UN MINURSO, and ongoing sovereignty dispute.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Western Sahara's sovereignty dispute has led to a significant regional impact, with ongoing tensions between Morocco and the Polisario Front affecting North Africa's politics and economy. The territory's phosphate resources have also been a point of contention.
